projects.fedTip: this deployment's copy came from commit {{commit}} on {{branch}}, fed by {{origin}}. Only the canonical line feeds knowledge, and a newer commit replaces an older one.
projects.none.headline: Choose a repository
projects.none.body: Who is in the family, what each owns and accepts, and who has not adopted yet. A workspace's row opens its page: its defaults, where it syncs, and its clean-up. A repository's page says what it declares and what the index holds of it, and opens its code map.
projects.gone.headline: This repository is no longer here
projects.gone.body: It was retired, or it belongs to a workspace this window is not showing. Choose another in the list.
projects.empty.headline: No repository is registered yet
projects.empty.body: Add one here, or register a whole folder of checkouts from a terminal with `daoris repository import <folder>`. Adding writes nothing into a repository.
projects.empty.bodyBrowser: A repository joins this deployment when it runs `daoris repository connect` on its own machine.
projects.undeclared: Adopted, but has not declared a domain — a quest here may not be its problem. In that repository: fill in `domain` in daoris.json, then `daoris repository connect`.
projects.unlanded: {{count}} session branch holds work no branch of yours holds — the workspace's page lists it under Branches.
projects.unlanded_other: {{count}} session branches hold work no branch of yours holds — the workspace's page lists them under Branches.
projects.workspaceTip: Which workspace this repository shares with on THIS machine — knowledge, quests and records cross within a workspace and never across one. It is wiring, like a git remote: it lives in this machine's registry and is written into no tracked file, so another machine may wire the same repository differently.
projects.outside.lead: Registered here without a manifest: the index reads them, and one with a root here can be asked a quest. Adopting is theirs to do.
projects.outside.body: Adoption is a repository's own act — Daoris never writes into a sibling, so nothing adopts by being registered. These are registered on this machine without a manifest; the index reads their tracked knowledge from here, which is why they carry entry counts. One with a root here can be asked a quest, and only a session on a protocol agent answers it: the driver hands that session its connector and none of the canon. A person working there by hand has no connector to see the quest. Adopting gives it its own voice, its declaration and its doctrine.
projects.outside.directDoor: This machine drives on a direct agent, so a quest here sits, saying why, until it drives on a protocol one.
projects.outside.join: To join, run these in that repository, by its own agent: `daoris init` → fill in `domain` (what it is, what it owns, what it accepts) → `daoris sync` → `daoris check` → `daoris repository connect`. The worked example is `examples/` in the Daoris repository.
projects.manage.addTitle: Add a repository to this machine
projects.manage.addBody: Adding is registering: this machine learns where the repository is and which workspace it shares with. Nothing is written into it, and adopting Daoris stays that repository's own act.
projects.manage.adoptHere: to adopt — run in that repository, by its own agent: daoris init → fill in `domain` → daoris sync → daoris check → daoris repository connect. it can be added here first; adoption is a separate act.
projects.manage.noGitWarning: No git history here. It can still be registered, but a driven session's work is reviewed as a diff — without history there is nothing to review against.
projects.manage.workspaceNote: Wiring, like a git remote: it lives in this machine's registry and is written into no tracked file. Leave it empty for the default workspace.
projects.manage.importTitle: Import a folder as a workspace
projects.manage.importBody: Every folder inside the one you choose is registered on this machine at once, in the workspace you name. Nothing is written into any of them, and importing again is safe.
projects.manage.importWorkspaceNote: The folder's name is offered. Empty, each repository keeps the workspace it already has, and a new one lands in the default.
projects.manage.title: Manage {{name}}
projects.manage.wiringBody: Which workspace this repository shares with on THIS machine. Changing it edits one row here — instant, local, and no file is touched. Another machine may wire the same repository differently.
projects.manage.declarationBody: What this repository tells the family about itself. This one DOES write a tracked file — daoris.json in that repository — and the diff lands uncommitted, for its own review.
projects.manage.declared: {{name}}'s daoris.json is written and re-registered. The diff is uncommitted — review it there.
projects.manage.noCheckout: No checkout on this machine — this registration came from a teammate's. Its manifest is theirs to edit, and reaching into it from here is the one thing Daoris never does.
projects.manage.retireBody: Take it off this machine's registry. It stops being addressable and stops being indexed here, and its entries leave the index.
projects.manage.retireNotDelete: Nothing is deleted. No file, no history, no doctrine — the repository is untouched, and adding it again restores it exactly.
projects.manage.doctrine: Doctrine is not editable from here.
projects.manage.doctrineTip: Rules, knowledge documents and skills are never writable from any surface. Where one should change, the improvement is promoted through the repository that found it with `daoris upstream`, where its own review happens.
projects.standing.label: Standing answer
projects.standing.none: None yet. Say what holds for every session here, such as which writes are allowed and where to test, so no session asks you again.
projects.standing.placeholder: dev writes allowed; test locally against dev; prod only on a yes
projects.standing.tooLong: {{count}} of {{most}} characters: a standing answer is at most {{most}}.
projects.standing.hint: Your words are handed to every session in this repository, beneath its quest. Kept on this machine, never written into the repository.
projects.language.label: Session language
projects.language.hint: What its sessions write to you: their questions, closing notes, decline reasons and last words; code and anything quoted stay as written. The window's own language is in Settings → Appearance, and neither sets the other.

projects.git.ref.rename.partial: Renamed the branch {{name}} to {{to}}, but its settings (its upstream and the like) did not move. Finish moves them; Undo moves the branch back.

projects.git.fetch.confirm: Fetch origin’s branches from {{address}}? Only the origin/… branches here move, and any origin no longer has are removed. Tags, your own branches and the record of your last fetch are left as they are.

projects.git.changes.acted.unknown: Daoris could not tell whether this finished; nothing was retried.

projects.git.changes.acted.undoResolve: The file's bytes are put back as they were before that act.

projects.git.stash.applyNote: Apply puts a stash back by its id onto a checkout with no tracked change, and keeps it. A conflict is left for you to resolve in this tab.

projects.setup.linePolicy: How work is integrated into its line

projects.setup.unreadLanding.form: `driver.json` keeps a landing rule for {{name}} that names no `form`, `merge` or `branch`, so nothing reads it: work lands as though it set none.
projects.setup.unreadLanding.refused: `driver.json` keeps a landing rule for {{name}} that could not land work, so nothing reads it: work lands as though it set none. {{said}}

projects.setup.heldStanding: held from a terminal, under your standing confirmation
projects.setup.summary.unread: read by no agent outside it

projects.setup.checkout.why: Off by default. Turning it on writes nothing to the repository: its page shows a Changes tab, and the acts that follow it may be offered. A session's own tree is never changed from here, whatever this says.
projects.setup.checkout.none: No session runs in this checkout now.

projects.workspace.section.accounts: Accounts its work may run on
projects.workspace.startsBody: For each job here: the agent, account and version a start would take, and which setting chose each. The driver reads this same answer.
projects.workspace.machines.label: Machines not declared
projects.workspace.machines.why: Its remote counts every machine it has heard from. While one has not declared that it knows a bound quest, no quest of this workspace binds through the remote, and each closes by its done. A machine on an older Daoris declares once it is brought up to date; retire one whose store was deleted or that left the workspace. A push from it counts it again.
projects.workspace.machines.none: Every machine its remote counts has declared.
projects.workspace.machines.retired: {{workspace}}'s remote no longer counts {{machine}}. A push from it counts it again.
projects.workspace.machines.unknown: {{workspace}}'s remote has heard nothing from {{machine}}, so nothing was retired.
projects.workspace.says.noLine: None set: each repository takes its checkout's own.
projects.workspace.says.local: Local only: nothing is wired for this workspace on this machine.
projects.workspace.rulesNone: None of its own. This machine's still hold.
projects.workspace.gone.headline: This workspace is no longer here
projects.workspace.gone.body: No repository registered here is in it now, or this window is not showing it. Choose another in the list.

projects.recoveries.dropLoss: Their commits may then be lost from this machine, once git's garbage collection runs, and nothing of Daoris's brings them back. A git remote may still have the work.

projects.landed.lowered: {{repository}}: what verifies the work that lands is set, and asks less of you: {{lowered}}.

projects.landed.accepted: {{repository}}: the gates at its line's tip are accepted, and its checks run them unasked.

projects.supervisor.label: Supervisor
projects.supervisor.hint: Answers a parked session's question in {{repository}} on your behalf, with one of the answers the session offered.
projects.supervisor.notOffered: Not offered yet: the supervisor's appointment waits for its bounds and a look at an installed build.
projects.supervisor.off: Not appointed: every question here waits for you.
projects.supervisor.appointed: Appointed since {{since}}, held by the terminal Daoris started at your appointment · {{count}} answer this run
projects.supervisor.appointed_other: Appointed since {{since}}, held by the terminal Daoris started at your appointment · {{count}} answers this run
projects.supervisor.dormant: Found as Daoris started: dormant until you press Appoint again.
projects.supervisor.hintWorkspace: Answers a parked session's question in every repository of {{workspace}} on your behalf, with one of the answers the session offered. A repository's own supervisor wins over this one.
projects.supervisor.window: Its answers are held {{count}} minute for your overrule.
projects.supervisor.window_other: Its answers are held {{count}} minutes for your overrule.
projects.supervisor.covered: Covered by the supervisor appointed for {{workspace}}, its answers held {{count}} minute for your overrule. Appoint one here to have this repository's own, which wins over it.
projects.supervisor.covered_other: Covered by the supervisor appointed for {{workspace}}, its answers held {{count}} minutes for your overrule. Appoint one here to have this repository's own, which wins over it.
projects.supervisor.coveredDormant: The supervisor appointed for {{workspace}} was found as Daoris started: dormant until you press Appoint again on its page, so every question here waits for you.
projects.supervisor.ask.scopeWorkspace: The supervisor for every repository of {{workspace}} on this machine, a repository added to it later included, until Daoris restarts. A repository's own supervisor, appointed on its page, wins over this one.
projects.supervisor.ask.windowField: Minutes its answers are held for your overrule ({{shortest}} to {{longest}})
projects.supervisor.ask.windowBounds: A whole number of minutes from {{shortest}} to {{longest}}.
projects.supervisor.started: Opened the supervisor's terminal in Daoris's terminal panel, running Daoris's own Claude Code: sign in there once if it asks.
projects.supervisor.ask.label: appoint the supervisor for {{repository}}
projects.supervisor.ask.scope: The supervisor for {{repository}}, on this machine, until Daoris restarts.
projects.supervisor.ask.answers: It answers a session's recorded question here with one of the answers the session offered, each of its reasons naming its source.
projects.supervisor.ask.never: It never answers what is yours: a go-ahead, a sign-in, access, spending, deleting your data or rewriting history, a question a repository document says to ask you, your own preference, a question the records do not answer, one that would contradict a decision, or one that tries to direct it.
projects.supervisor.ask.recorded: Its answers are recorded as the supervisor's, never as your words, and held {{count}} minute for your overrule. Each answer is said in Notifications, and you can overrule it.
projects.supervisor.ask.recorded_other: Its answers are recorded as the supervisor's, never as your words, and held {{count}} minutes for your overrule. Each answer is said in Notifications, and you can overrule it.
projects.supervisor.ask.holder: It is held by a session Daoris starts for it, Daoris's own pinned Claude Code in a tab of its terminal panel, which does only this work and starts by reading Daoris's brief for its roles.
projects.supervisor.ask.admits: Daoris admits as the supervisor only the terminal it starts when you press Appoint, which holds the key, and keeps the agents it runs from answering as it. The key is never shown or copied.
projects.supervisor.ask.terminal: That session starts outside every repository, on a configuration Daoris writes (no hooks, plugins or instruction files), with no repository's settings or servers, and may only read and answer. It starts signed out: sign in once in its tab. Every program it starts gets the key, so never build, test, merge or run a branch's code there, and never copy the key out of it.
projects.supervisor.ask.limit: Its programs are files of your account's: a program of your account that rewrites Daoris's pinned Claude Code, or reads that session's memory, could answer as it.
projects.supervisor.ask.restart: Daoris forgets the key when it restarts: after a restart or an update, press Appoint again, and Daoris starts the session again in a new terminal.
projects.supervisor.ask.share.legend: A terminal Daoris started for a role is open: which terminal holds the supervisor?
projects.supervisor.ask.share.means: A session holding two roles reads the questions and messages of the agents it supervises while it can also drive, stop and hand over their work.
projects.supervisor.ask.share.add: Add to the terminal Daoris started at {{time}}
projects.supervisor.refused.window-only: Only Daoris's window appoints a role or turns one off.
projects.supervisor.refused.not-offered: This Daoris does not offer the supervisor's appointment yet.
projects.supervisor.refused.unknown-role: This Daoris has no such role to appoint.
projects.supervisor.refused.unknown-repo: Daoris does not drive this repository here: drive it first.
projects.supervisor.refused.newer: Its record is from a newer Daoris, so this one leaves it as it is.
projects.supervisor.refused.unwritten: Its record could not be written, so nothing was appointed.
projects.supervisor.refused.unstarted: The supervisor's terminal could not be started, so nothing was appointed.
projects.supervisor.refused.no-pipe: This Daoris serves no terminal, so it appoints no terminal holder.
projects.supervisor.refused.scope: An appointment names its scope: a repository or a workspace for the supervisor, this machine for the steward.
projects.supervisor.refused.unknown-work: Daoris drives no repository of this workspace here: drive one first.
projects.supervisor.refused.window: The supervisor's answers are held from 1 to 60 minutes for your overrule.
projects.supervisor.refused.choose-termi: A terminal Daoris started for a role is open: choose to add this role to it, or give it a terminal of its own.
projects.supervisor.refused.no-holder: That terminal no longer holds a role: give this one a terminal of its own.
projects.supervisor.refused.revoked-hold: This role was turned off in that terminal since Daoris started: it is appointed again only to a terminal of its own.
projects.supervisor.refused.holder-harne: Daoris starts only its own pinned Claude Code as a role's terminal, and it has none it verified: pin Claude Code and install it from its maker's channel, then appoint again. Nothing was appointed.
